stage_fields.problem_definition: Given a multiple-sequence alignment of ~5000 fast-evolving viral genomes (CPU-only, Python/BioPython, no pre-built phylogeny or nomenclature assumed), infer for each genome whether it is mosaic and, if so, the breakpoint coordinates and the parent-cluster assignment of each segment — at a scale and per-genome cost the triplet-scan (3SEQ/RDP5) and topology-search (GARD) classics do not reach.
stage_fields.estimand: Per genome i in a ~5000-genome multiple-sequence alignment of a fast-evolving virus: (a) a binary mosaic label z_i in {0,1}; (b) IF z_i=1, the ordered set of breakpoint genomic coordinates B_i = (b_i1, ..., b_ik) (k>=1) and the parent-cluster assignment c_i(w) in {1..C} for each inter-breakpoint segment w, i.e. which clade/lineage each segment of genome i is derived from. Over target_population = future samplings of the same viral species at comparable diversity. This is the mosaic-structure + breakpoint-location + parent-assignment estimand, NOT a yes/no 'is there recombination in the alignment'.
stage_fields.mathematical_abstraction: Fundamentally a CHANGE-POINT DETECTION problem on a sequence of nearest-neighbor-graph membership profiles along the genome. A non-recombinant genome has a CONSTANT parent-cluster assignment across genome windows; a mosaic genome has one or more CHANGE-POINTS where the assignment switches between parent clusters. (Rejected: (1) phylogenetic-tree-rebuilding per partition (GARD) — global topology search does not scale to 5000 genomes on CPU and is sensitive to substitution-model mis-specification; (2) all-triplets enumeration (3SEQ/RDP5) — O(n^2) to O(n^3) in genome count, the cited reason these tools 'do not scale to big data' (Alfonsi 2024, Nat Comms); (3) data-driven lineage-mutation-space scoring (RecombinHunt) — requires a structured nomenclature + >=3 supporting mutations, a slot the user does not have.) The change-point-on-similarity-profile view keeps the failure boundary (homoplasy vs recombination) explicit and gives a per-genome linear-cost scan instead of an all-pairs/triplets scan.

symbols.A: alignment, n genomes x L alignment columns, alphabet {A,C,G,T,-}
symbols.L: alignment length (~9.8 kb HIV / ~29.9 kb SARS-CoV-2)
symbols.n_win: number of tiling windows (~ L / win_size; win_size ~ 200-400 nt)
symbols.D: per-window row of distance computations reused across genomes
symbols.S_i: similarity profile of genome i: S_i[w,j] = normalized similarity (1 - p-distance) of genome i to genome j within window w
symbols.G_w: kNN graph at window w (sparse, top-k neighbors per node)
symbols.c_i: parent-cluster membership of genome i per window, c_i[w] in 1..C
symbols.C: number of parent clusters (~ number of clades/lineages)
symbols.B_i: ordered breakpoint coordinate vector for genome i (length k_i)
symbols.k_i: number of breakpoints in genome i (0 => non-recombinant)
symbols.P: per-segment parent-cluster path (vector of length k_i+1, one parent id per segment of genome i; indexed alongside B_i)
symbols.Q: C x L cluster consensus subtitution patterns (used in the discordance test)
symbols.M: n x C hard cluster assignment at the whole-genome level

assumptions: Substitutions are approximately Poisson/Jukes-Cantor within a window at the species' diversity scale (used only to convert p-distance to a normalized similarity; the method degrades gracefully if rate heterogeneity is strong — see failure boundary FB-HOMOPLASY).

Within each true (non-recombinant) clade, between-genome p-distance in a window is stochastically dominated by between-clade p-distance (clades are separable in local similarity). This is the cluster-separability assumption; if it fails (FB-WEAK-CLUSTERING) detection loses power.

Recombination, when present, produces a SEGMENT (>= ~win_size) of genome whose nearest-neighbor cluster differs from the flanking segments. Tracts shorter than win_size are not resolvable (FB-SHORT-TRACT).

A recombination breakpoint is a step-change in parent-cluster assignment; gradual introgression / gene-conversion tracts are modeled as a single segment with a half-window boundary uncertainty (not a separate mechanism).
No recombination => c_i is constant in w (the null model). This is the null regime the method must NOT reject.

stage_fields.objective_or_likelihood: For each genome i, define the per-window best-parent-similarity trace  r_i[w] = max_c (mean over members j of cluster c of S_i[w,j])  in R^{n_win}, i.e. for each window the similarity of genome i to its best-matching parent cluster. Under the null (single parent, no recombination) r_i[w] is piecewise-constant in w up to finite-sample noise; a recombination event is a step change in the level of r_i at the breakpoint. The objective is a penalized LEAST-SQUARES segmented-Gaussian change-point on r_i (the natural model for a sample-mean trace with additive noise):  argmax_{k_i, B_i}  [ -(1/2 sigma^2) sum_{s=0}^{k_i} sum_{w in segment s} (r_i[w] - mu_s)^2 ]  -  lambda * k_i * log(n_win)   where mu_s is the per-segment mean of r_i (the within-segment best-parent similarity), sigma^2 is the empirical within-segment variance, lambda is FIXED at 1 (so the penalty is the standard BIC/MDL term k_i * log(n_win), used purely for MODEL SELECTION of the breakpoint count), and k_i, B_i are the count and positions of breakpoints. This is the Gaussian change-point family (Adams & MacKay 2007 Bayesian online CPD; Killick et al. 2012 PELT; scikit-learn / ruptures Dynp/Binseg) applied to the similarity trace, NOT a categorical likelihood on the n-dim similarity vector. The null (k_i=0, single mean) is tested against the k_i>=1 alternative by a likelihood-ratio statistic whose REJECTION THRESHOLD is calibrated on the null DGP to control genome-level FPR at alpha (separate from lambda: lambda selects the model given a breakpoint is present; the calibrated threshold decides WHETHER a breakpoint is present). Parent-cluster assignments per segment c_i(w) are recovered post-hoc as argmax_c of the segment's mean similarity to each cluster.
stage_fields.identifiability: NOT identifiable without the discordance correction: a change in nearest-neighbor cluster along the genome can be caused by (a) true recombination, (b) shared ancestry with local rate variation, or (c) homoplasy / convergent evolution under high divergence (substitution saturation). Cases (b) and (c) are the confounds named in trap T4. Identifiable ONLY when the two candidate parent segments are PHYLOGENETICALLY DISCORDANT — i.e. placing the two segments of genome i onto a single best-fit tree is significantly less likely than placing them onto two different trees (a two-tree vs one-tree likelihood-ratio test, the same statistical move GARD uses, but applied locally per candidate recombinant rather than globally per alignment). The additional assumption that restores identifiability: the two parent clusters are on sufficiently diverged parts of the tree that within-cluster site patterns are distinguishable from between-cluster site patterns (cluster separability). If the parent clusters are sisters / nearly identical (recent divergence), recombination from one into the other is NOT identifiable from this data alone — declared as failure boundary FB-WEAK-CLUSTERING, not papered over. The local two-tree-vs-one-tree test is the identifiability handle; without it the change-point detector would fire on pure homoplasy.
stage_fields.cross_domain_inspiration: Engaged (2 domains outside phylogenetics/virology): (1) STATISTICAL PROCESS CONTROL / Bayesian online change-point detection (Adams & MacKay 2007, from finance/quality-control run-length distributions) — the segmented-likelihood + run-length posterior is the core change-point machinery applied to similarity-profile 'time series' where genome-coordinate plays the role of time. Selected because the per-genome scan is exactly a 1-D ordered sequence with piecewise-constant latent state. (2) GRAPH SIGNAL PROCESSING / spectral graph theory (graph-Fourier / normalized-cut image segmentation, Shi-Malik 2000) — the parent-cluster discovery step uses a normalized-cut / spectral embedding of the per-window kNN graph G_w to discover C latent parent clusters without a pre-built tree, instead of requiring a nomenclature (the RecombinHunt slot) or a global phylogeny (the RIPPLES slot). Discarded spark: compressed-sensing sparse-recovery (the change-point vector is sparse but the measurement matrix is not incoherent across highly correlated clades, so CS gives no edge); hidden-Markov-model on raw sequence columns (an HMM over alignment columns would entangle recombination with rate variation and was rejected in favor of operating on the derived similarity-profile where the two are separable by the discordance test).
stage_fields.proposed_algorithm: RECOMB-CP (Recombination as Change-Points on similarity profiles). Steps: (1) LOAD — read MSA with BioPython AlignIO (A, shape n x L); drop all-gap columns; encode as uint8. (2) WINDOW — tile the alignment into n_win overlapping windows of win_size (~300 nt) with step ~win_size/2; build the per-window distance row D. (3) PER-GENOME SIMILARITY PROFILE — for each genome i, for each window w, compute the normalized similarity S_i[w,j] = 1 - p-distance(i,j within w) to all other genomes j (vectorized Hamming over the uint8 window block, O(n_win * n * win_size) total via numpy broadcasting, NOT O(n^2) all-pairs per window because each (i,w) is an independent row scan). (4) PARENT-CLUSTER DISCOVERY — at each window w, build a sparse kNN graph G_w (k~15) on S_i[w,:]; aggregate across windows into a single consensus affinity matrix M (n x C via spectral normalized-cut with C estimated from the eigengap). C is the number of parent clusters; M[i,c] is genome i's whole-genome parent cluster. (5) PER-GENOME MEMBERSHIP PATH — c_i[w] = argmax_c (mean similarity of genome i to members of cluster c within window w), giving the per-window parent-cluster membership sequence c_i in {1..C}^{n_win}. (6) CHANGE-POINT DETECTION — for each genome i, run the segmented-likelihood maximization (dynamic programming over breakpoint positions with the BIC penalty) on c_i (or, equivalently, on the soft similarity profile) to get candidate breakpoint set B_i and segment assignments. (7) DISCORDANCE TEST (the recombination-vs-homoplasy identifiability correction) — for each candidate recombinant with k_i>=1, compute the two-tree vs one-tree local likelihood ratio on the two segment alignments (small ML tree per segment via a Bio.Phylo / lightweight JC-distance NJ, NOT a global phylogeny); keep the breakpoint only if the two-tree model is significantly better (Bonferroni-corrected LRT). (8) NULL CALIBRATION — declare mosaic only if the segmented-vs-null likelihood ratio exceeds a threshold calibrated on the null DGP to hold the genome-level false-positive rate at a target alpha (default 1%). (9) OUTPUT — per genome: z_i, B_i, c_i segments, a confidence score (the LRT statistic), and a low-signal flag when the supporting-segment mutation count < tau.
stage_fields.optimization_or_inference: Decomposed into two independent optima, both with guarantees: (A) the per-genome change-point step is solved EXACTLY by dynamic programming over a discrete breakpoint-position grid (O(n_win^2) per genome for the standard segmented-likelihood DP, or O(n_win) with the Pruned Exact Linear Time / FPOP-style pruning for the Poisson-ish special case); DP on a 1-D segmentation with a BIC penalty is globally optimal (convex in the segment-means given the breakpoint count, and the breakpoint count is regularized by the penalty) — no local minima, no initialization sensitivity. (B) the parent-cluster discovery step is a spectral normalized-cut solved by an eigendecomposition of the symmetric normalized graph Laplacian (global optimum of the relaxed Ncut objective; k-means on the top-C eigenvectors gives the discrete assignment, standard spectral clustering). The discordance test is a fixed chi-square LRT. Convergence: step (A) terminates in O(n_win^2) ops deterministically; step (B) terminates in one eigendecomposition + one k-means (k-means seeded by k-means++ for reproducibility). Stopping: DP has a closed-form solution; no iteration. Total: deterministic, no SGD, no random initialization in the core path (k-means seeding is the only RNG and is fixed by seed).
stage_fields.complexity: Per-genome cost is LINEAR in genome count (not quadratic/triplet): the similarity-profile build is O(n_win * n * win_size) per genome (vectorized Hamming) and the change-point DP is O(n_win^2) per genome; the discordance test is O(C_pairs * L_seg) (small NJ trees per segment, segment length L_seg << L). Total over all genomes: O(n * n_win * n * win_size) for the all-profiles build dominates (this is the same cost as ONE all-pairs Hamming pass), + O(n * n_win^2) for all change-point DPs, + O(n_recomb * L) for the discordance tests (only on candidates). For n=5000, L=30kb, win_size=300, n_win~200: the all-profiles pass is ~5000*5000*200*300 = 1.5e12 byte-ops worst case but VECTORIZED and reducible to a single numpy Hamming over the uint8 alignment (~7.5 GB peak for one window-row block, streamed); the DP is 5000*200^2 = 2e8 ops (seconds). The bottleneck is the similarity-profile build, mitigated by (i) streaming one window at a time (memory O(n) per window, not O(n*n_win)), (ii) kNN sparsification (keep top-k=15 not all-n), (iii) optional LSH/MinHash pre-screen for the top-k neighbors. Memory footprint: O(n*L) for the alignment (~150 MB uint8 for 5000x30kb) + O(n*k) per window graph. CPU-feasible to ~10^4 genomes on a laptop; ~5000 is the design point. Contrast: 3SEQ all-triplets is O(n^3) in genome count (n=5000 => 1.25e11 triplets) and GARD's global topology search is the cited reason it does not scale (Alfonsi 2024).

failure_boundaries.condition: High divergence => substitution saturation: between-clade site patterns become non-informative (multiple hits per site), so convergent changes mimic a parent-cluster switch.
failure_boundaries.mechanism: Under saturation the per-window p-distance underestimates true divergence and the similarity profile S_i[w,j] becomes dominated by shared convergent sites; the change-point detector fires on the homoplasious cluster switch, and the two-tree-vs-one-tree discordance test loses power because the per-segment site patterns are no longer distinguishable. Detected by a per-window saturation diagnostic (entropy of the substitution pattern / site; high entropy => saturated); genomes/windows flagged saturated are reported as unresolvable, not as recombinant.

failure_boundaries.condition: Recombinant tract length < win_size (~300 nt) or supported by < tau mutations (~3).
failure_boundaries.mechanism: The windowed similarity profile cannot resolve a tract shorter than one window (the change is averaged out within the window), and the segmented likelihood cannot place a breakpoint more precisely than ~win_size/2. By the uncertainty principle of windowed analysis, short tracts are absorbed into the flanking segment's parent assignment. Reported as a hard detection floor (the method reports 'no breakpoint >= win_size'; sub-window tracts are a known limitation, matching RecombinHunt's <3-mutation limit).

failure_boundaries.condition: Parent clusters are very recently diverged (sister clades), so within-cluster and between-cluster site patterns overlap.
failure_boundaries.mechanism: The cluster-separability assumption fails: the spectral normalized-cut does not separate the two parents, M merges them into one cluster, and c_i is constant (no change-point) even though a true recombination occurred. The two-tree-vs-one-tree LRT has no power because the two segment trees are nearly identical. Recombination between near-identical parents is NOT identifiable from this data alone — reported as a known limitation (requires denser sampling or an outgroup), not a false negative hidden in the output.

failure_boundaries.condition: Alignment has high gap/ambiguity (N-content) density in a region.
failure_boundaries.mechanism: Gappy windows have few informative sites; the per-window p-distance is biased (overestimates distance uniformly) and the similarity profile is noisy; the change-point DP over-segments in noisy regions producing spurious breakpoints. Mitigated by a per-window informative-site-count gate (windows below a threshold are masked / interpolated); if a candidate breakpoint falls in a gappy window it is down-weighted or flagged low-confidence.

failure_boundaries.condition: Substitution rate varies along the genome (gamma-distributed site rates / known hypervariable regions, e.g. SARS-CoV-2 Spike, HIV env V-loops) WITHOUT recombination and WITHOUT convergent evolution.
failure_boundaries.mechanism: Under rate heterogeneity alone, a genome's nearest-neighbor cluster can shift across windows simply because fast-evolving regions accumulate more substitutions locally, so c_i[w] is NOT constant even in a truly non-recombinant genome — the null 'no recombination => c_i constant' is violated by rate variation, not just by homoplasy (FB-HOMOPLASY covers saturation/convergence; this boundary covers the distinct pure-rate-variation confound). The change-point detector over-segments in hypervariable regions producing false breakpoints. Mitigated by (i) calibrating the null DGP with a Gamma rate prior (+I+Gamma) so the FPR threshold accounts for rate variation, (ii) optionally using a rate-corrected distance (paralinear/GTR) in the NN graph, and (iii) the discordance test requiring the two segments to be phylogenetically discordant BEYOND what a single-tree + rate-heterogeneity model explains (the two-tree LRT null is one-tree WITH rate heterogeneity, not one-tree JC69).

stage_fields.uncertainty_and_calibration: Each reported breakpoint carries (i) a likelihood-ratio statistic (the margin by which the k_i>=1 model beats the null), converted to a genome-level p-value calibrated on the null DGP to control FDR via Benjamini-Hochberg across the ~5000 genomes; (ii) a coordinate-uncertainty interval of ~half-window (the DP places the breakpoint within one window). Coverage of the breakpoint-coordinate interval is evaluated on the simulation DGP (target: the true breakpoint lies in the reported interval in >=90% of true-recombinant cases). Calibration is RELATIVE to the DGP, not absolute, because real-data recombination truth is unavailable; reported as a calibrated-under-DGP quantity, not a coverage-guaranteed CI.
stage_fields.invariances: Invariant to: genome-index permutation (the scan is per-genome and symmetric), cluster-label permutation (spectral clustering labels are arbitrary), and alignment-column permutation WITHIN a window (the window is summarized by p-distance which is column-order-invariant). NOT invariant to: window-size choice (changes the detection floor, FB-SHORT-TRACT), gap-handling (changes per-window distance, see FB-GAPPY), and outgroup inclusion (changes the cluster tree and the discordance test power).
stage_fields.simulation_dgp: DGP: a coalescent-with-recombination simulator (SCOT-style / SimBac-style / sc2ts-style for SARS-CoV-2; or a controlled synthetic DGP: simulate K parent clades under JC69 on a star tree, draw intra-clade diversity to match the target virus' pairwise-distance distribution, then inject recombinants by splicing a segment of length L_tract from a donor clade into an acceptor genome at a known breakpoint, then re-mutate under JC69). Regimes: (NULL) no recombinants injected => method must return z_i=0 for all genomes (false-positive rate <= alpha=1%, the no-hallucination test). (ADVERSARIAL-HOMOPLASY) inject convergent-evolution tracts (same substitutions in unrelated clades, NOT a true recombination) => method must NOT call them recombinant (tests the FB-HOMOPLASY discordance correction). (ADVERSARIAL-SHORT-TRACT) inject tracts of length {win_size/4, win_size/2, win_size, 2*win_size} => measure the detection floor (tests FB-SHORT-TRACT). (ADVERSARIAL-WEAK) inject recombination between sister clades at divergence {0.1%, 0.5%, 1%, 5%} => measure power loss (tests FB-WEAK-CLUSTERING). (ADVERSARIAL-GAPPY) inject random gaps/Ns at {0, 5%, 20%, 40%} density => measure robustness (tests FB-GAPPY). (ORACLE) give the method the true parent-cluster labels => upper bound on breakpoint-localization accuracy. (TRIVIAL) a single-breakpoint + a constant-assignment naive baseline and a no-recombination-at-all baseline => lower bounds. Swept parameters: n in {500, 2000, 5000}, L_tract, divergence, gap-density, recombinant fraction in {1%, 5%, 15%}, win_size in {200, 300, 500}.
stage_fields.benchmark_protocol: Competitors (same MSA input, same held-out evaluation, same compute budget, same pre-processing — gap-trimming, identical sub-column sampling): NAIVE baselines (Category 5, MUST beat): (a) no-recombination null (calls everything non-recombinant), (b) single-global-breakpoint scan (one breakpoint per genome max, the simplest change-point), (c) raw nearest-neighbor switch without the discordance test (the ablation that isolates the homoplasy-correction's contribution). SOTA (Category 1 functional substitutes): 3SEQ (Lam 2018 improved, mol.ax/software/3seq), RDP5 (Martin 2021, the 7-method suite; run its Bootscan + MaxChi + 3SEQ modules), GARD (HyPhy, pond 2006). SCALING (Category 1, different regime): RecombinHunt (Alfonsi 2024) IF a Pango-style nomenclature is available (otherwise it is an input-slot alternative, Category 3, for this user), RIPPLES/RIVET (Turakhia 2022) IF a global phylogeny is pre-built (otherwise also Cat 3). Metrics: per-genome mosaic detection (precision, recall, F1 at FDR<=5%), breakpoint-localization accuracy (mean |b_hat - b_true| in nt; fraction within win_size/2), parent-assignment accuracy (fraction of segments assigned to the true donor clade), FPR on the null DGP (must be <= alpha), runtime and peak memory at n in {500, 2000, 5000}. Fairness: identical MSAs, identical gap-trimming, identical random seeds, compute-matched (cap wall-clock, report CPU-hours); competitors run with their default/recommended settings; no method-specific tuning advantage. Leakage guard (trap T2/T3): held-out recombinant events use FRESH parent pairs not in the fitting set; truth comes ONLY from the simulator (NEVER from another detection method — circular ground truth, trap T3). Multiple seeds per condition, report mean +/- sd.
stage_fields.novelty_or_utility_basis: Utility first, novelty explicit. Novelty locus: a NEW INFERENCE MECHANISM for this estimand at this scale — recombination as change-point detection on per-genome nearest-neighbor-graph membership profiles, with a local two-tree-vs-one-tree discordance test as the recombination-vs-homoplasy identifiability correction, replacing the all-triplets scan (3SEQ/RDP5) and the global-topology search (GARD). The estimand (mosaic label + breakpoint coordinates + parent assignment) and the broad likelihood-ratio idea are shared with prior work; the novelty is (1) the per-genome LINEAR-cost scan on similarity profiles (vs O(n^2)/O(n^3) triplet scans) making the ~5000-genome CPU regime tractable, (2) operating on the derived similarity-profile rather than raw columns so recombination is separable from rate variation via the discordance test, and (3) NOT requiring a pre-built global phylogeny (RIPPLES slot) or a structured nomenclature (RecombinHunt slot). Tier: T2 — defensibly better than the named top_competitors on the SCALABILITY axis (CPU-feasible at n=5000 where 3SEQ/RDP5/GARD are documented not to scale) and on the NO-PHYLOGENY/NO-NOMENCLATURE input-slot axis, under a fair benchmark that includes the naive single-breakpoint and no-recombination baselines. NOT claimed as T1 structural novelty: it is a rigorous combination of change-point detection (Adams-MacKay) + spectral graph clustering (normalized cut) + a local phylogenetic-discordance LRT (GARD's move applied locally), not a new estimand or a new objective family. Deltas vs named top_competitors: vs 3SEQ/RDP5 (Cat 1) — per-genome O(n) not O(n^2)/O(n^3); CPU-feasible at 5000 genomes; explicit homoplasy-failure boundary where 3SEQ/RDP5 report a breakpoint unconditionally. vs GARD (Cat 1) — local per-genome LRT instead of global topology search; GARD's documented non-scaling (crashes on 27 SARS-CoV-2 genomes, HyPhy issue #1731) is the regime this targets. vs RecombinHunt (Cat 1 if nomenclature present, Cat 3 if absent) — does not require a lineage mutation-space; works in the no-nomenclature slot the user occupies; lower sensitivity on nomenclature-rich SARS-CoV-2 data (a known trade-off, T2 not T1). vs RIPPLES/RIVET (Cat 1 if global phylogeny present, Cat 3 if absent) — does not require a pre-built global phylogeny; lower accuracy when a good global tree IS available (a known trade-off). vs the naive single-breakpoint + no-recombination baselines (Cat 5) — must beat them on breakpoint recall and on FPR-controlled mosaic F1; if it does not, the method has no utility (the kill-switch).

component_necessity.simpler_alternative: raw_nearest_neighbor_switch (call a breakpoint whenever the argmax parent changes between adjacent windows, no phylogenetic test)
component_necessity.retain_if: discordance_test beats raw_nearest_neighbor_switch on FALSE-POSITIVE RATE in the null + homoplasy-only regimes (where the simpler method hallucinates) WITHOUT losing >5% recall in the true-recombination regimes

current_result.reason: PRE-REGISTERED — decision pending the benchmark. The raw switch has no recombination-vs-homoplasy identifiability handle (the trap-T4 confound); the LRT is the only mechanism that addresses it. If on the null+homoplasy regimes the LRT does not reduce FPR, it is removed and the method becomes the naive baseline (no utility).

component_necessity.simpler_alternative: fixed_predefined_clusters (use the Pango/lineage labels as parent clusters when a nomenclature exists)
component_necessity.retain_if: spectral clustering matches or beats the fixed-label baseline on parent-assignment accuracy in the no-nomenclature regime AND is within 5% in the nomenclature-available regime
